title: Secure On-Premise Regulatory Compliance Analysis
business: Financial institutions requiring strict data residency for document analysis.
problem: High latency and data privacy concerns when sending sensitive client financial records to third-party cloud-hosted AI APIs.
solution: Deploying Llama models locally within a private data center using the official Llama CLI and model weights to ensure data never leaves the secure perimeter.
steps: Accept the Meta Llama license and request access to model weights via the official portal.
Install the Llama Models CLI using pip install llama-models in the secure environment.
Authenticate and download the desired model ID using llama-model download --source meta.
Configure the local inference environment with necessary dependencies including torch.
Execute the model using torchrun to manage multi-GPU parallelization for high-throughput document processing.
outcome: Full control over data processing pipelines with zero external network dependency for inference tasks.
limitation: Hardware resource requirements; local deployment necessitates significant GPU memory, which can be checked by monitoring VRAM usage during inference.

diagram.description: The flow from model acquisition to secure local inference.

code.content:
# Run inference with FP8 quantization to optimize memory usage
MODE=fp8_mixed
CHECKPOINT_DIR=~/.llama/checkpoints/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct
# Use torchrun to distribute the model across available GPUs
torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 -m models.llama4.scripts.chat_completion $CHECKPOINT_DIR --quantization-mode $MODE
code.explanation: This script demonstrates how to run a Llama model locally using the provided CLI utilities and quantization flags to manage hardware constraints.
